Training Zones Calculator

Work out your cycling power zones from your FTP or a 20-minute test, and your heart-rate zones from your threshold heart rate.

Your numbers

I know

Threshold heart rate is your average heart rate for the last 20 minutes of a 30-minute solo all-out effort. Leave it empty if you don't know it.

Your zones

Enter your FTP or 20-minute power to see your zones.

How it works

HOW TO USE YOUR TRAINING ZONES

Training zones turn one number, your FTP, into clear targets for every session. Riding in the right zone makes sure an easy day is really easy and a hard day is hard enough to make you faster.

Power zones

These are the classic 7 power zones, each a percentage of your FTP. If you did a 20-minute test, your FTP is 95% of your average power for the 20 minutes.

  • Zones 1–2: recovery and endurance. Most of your weekly riding, building your aerobic base.
  • Zone 3: tempo. Steady and controlled, useful in long efforts and Gran Fondo pacing.
  • Zone 4: threshold. Intervals that raise your FTP.
  • Zones 5–7: VO2max, anaerobic and sprint. Short, very hard efforts.

Heart-rate zones

Heart rate reacts slowly and drifts with heat, tiredness and caffeine, so use it alongside power, or on its own if you don't have a power meter.

Keep your zones up to date

Your zones change as you get fitter. Re-test every 6 to 8 weeks. Our coached riders get adaptive zones that change every week, and testing with Critical Power or INSCYD, which goes beyond FTP.
